title: Control plane: emit v1 audit events for RBAC changes + API key lifecycle (with tests)
creator: Ethan Park
project: Audit Logging Standardization (Schema v1 + Sensitive Actions Coverage)
description:
## Summary
Instrument control plane services (tenant/config/policy/RBAC) to emit canonical audit events (schema v1) for:
- RBAC changes (roles, permissions, bindings/memberships)
- API key lifecycle (create, rotate, revoke, update metadata)

Includes unit + integration tests to prevent regressions and enforce required fields.

This is a gating item for “100% sensitive actions coverage” across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.

## Context / Why
Enterprise customers (especially Private) need consistent audit trails for identity and access management changes and credential lifecycle events. Current state:
- Some RBAC endpoints emit partial/legacy events, with inconsistent field names and missing correlation context.
- API key events are inconsistently captured and risk leaking sensitive material if not carefully redacted.

This work aligns control plane producers with:
- Canonical schema v1 (ENG-4821)
- Central event_type registry + lints (ENG-4822)
- Correlation standard (ENG-4830)

## In scope
### RBAC endpoints
Emit audit events for the following actions across org/tenant/project scopes (as applicable):
- Role created/updated/deleted
- Role binding / membership created/updated/deleted (user ↔ role, service account ↔ role)
- Permission set changes for a role (captured as diff summary)

### API key endpoints
Emit audit events for:
- API key created
- API key rotated (new key material issued)
- API key revoked
- API key name/description/labels updated (metadata-only update)

### Actor attribution requirements
For each event, populate:
- actor_type (user | service_account | system)
- actor_id (stable internal ID)
- actor_email (only when present in auth context; avoid for service accounts)
- impersonator_* fields when acting via admin impersonation / break-glass tooling
- source_ip and user_agent when available via gateway → control plane context propagation

### Target/resource modeling
Ensure target semantics are consistent:
- target_type: role | role_binding | api_key
- target_id: role_id / binding_id / api_key_id
- target_name: role name / key name (bounded length)
- resource_scope: org_id / tenant_id / project_id as applicable

### Sensitive data handling (must not log secrets)
For API keys:
- Never log key value, token prefix, full Authorization headers, or any derived value that could be used to reconstruct credentials.
- Permitted fields: key_id, key_name, key_last4 (optional), key_fingerprint (HMAC/SHA-256 truncated; only if already standard elsewhere), and key_scopes.
- Any “rotate” event must include only the new key_id (not the key material).

## Event types (registry)
Final event_type names registered (see ENG-4822 registry; aligned with taxonomy doc):
- rbac.role.created
- rbac.role.updated
- rbac.role.deleted
- rbac.binding.created
- rbac.binding.updated
- rbac.binding.deleted
- credential.api_key.created
- credential.api_key.rotated
- credential.api_key.revoked
- credential.api_key.updated

## Required schema fields (v1)
All emitted events must include:
- schema_version: "1.0"
- event_id: ULID (preferred) or UUIDv7 (accepted) generated at producer
- event_type
- event_time (RFC3339)
- deployment_mode: hosted | dedicated | private
- environment: prod | staging | dev
- org_id, tenant_id (when applicable), project_id (when applicable)
- actor_* (as above)
- target_* (as above)
- request_id + trace_id

Optional but strongly preferred for investigations:
- admin_action_id (stable across multi-step admin flows)
- change_summary (bounded string)
- change_diff_json (strictly bounded size; keys allow-listed; no arbitrary blobs)

## Implementation notes
- Producer: control-plane audit emitter wrapper using shared schema library + validator (from PR-21984).
- Emission is best-effort (do not block RBAC/API key operations on sink outage) but MUST:
  - increment metric audit_event_emit_failed_total{service, event_type, reason}
  - log structured error with request_id/trace_id (no sensitive payload)
- Cardinality guardrails:
  - role_name and key_name are length-capped and sanitized
  - permission lists are summarized (counts + allow-listed identifiers); no free-form strings

## Tests
### Unit tests
- For each handler/action, assert:
  - event_type matches registry
  - required fields present
  - redaction rules enforced (no key material in event)
  - validator passes against schema v1

### Integration tests
- Extend existing control-plane integration suite to execute:
  - create role → update permissions → delete role
  - create binding → change member → delete binding
  - create key → rotate key → revoke key
- Verify emitted events via test audit sink (in-memory collector) and assert:
  - ordering is not relied on (at-least-once / async); assert presence + correctness
  - correlation IDs match request context
  - dedupe guidance supported via stable event_id

## Rollout plan
1) Behind feature flag: audit.v1_control_plane_rbac_api_keys
2) Enable in staging for 1 week; monitor drop rate + validation failures
3) Enable in prod (Hosted/Dedicated) then Private default-on in next installer release window

## Links
- Schema library + validation: sources/github/redwood/pr-21984-add-audit-event-schema-library-and-validator.json
- RBAC events implementation: sources/github/redwood/pr-22005-control-plane-audit-events-rbac-changes.json
- API key lifecycle events implementation: sources/github/redwood/pr-22012-audit-events-api-key-lifecycle.json
- Correlation propagation: sources/github/redwood/pr-22047-audit-event-correlation-request-id-trace-id.json

## Acceptance criteria
- All RBAC + API key sensitive endpoints emit v1-shaped events with required fields.
- No credential material is present in events, logs, or metrics.
- Test suite includes integration coverage for the workflows above and runs in CI.
- Event types are registered and pass build-time lint rules.
- Verified parity across Hosted/Dedicated/Private (same control plane codepath; deployment_mode correctly set).

## Open questions / follow-ups
- Do we need explicit "credential.api_key.read" for admin views? (Currently out of scope; revisit with PM + Security to avoid noisy logs.)
- For bulk RBAC changes (future), confirm we want one event per mutation vs batched event with bounded diff list.

## Operational notes
- If audit sink is unavailable, operations proceed; we rely on metrics + alerts (ENG-4835) and incident runbook guidance.
- Producer includes a circuit-breaker to avoid cascading latency in control plane under audit sink failure.
